items.text: Last week, a government party MPLA claimed victory in Angola’s election; the party has ruled oil-rich Angola continuously for nearly 50 years. Only one day after the vote, the results were published with remarkable speed. In 2017, the last election numbers took two weeks to complete. Ex- Marxist MPLA had a solid majority after all votes were counted; however, the main opposition party cast doubt on the results. MPLA lost its majority in parliament, so it must cooperate with opposition lawmakers for the first time. Analysts fear that disputes will ignite violence among the poor and frustrated youth who voted for other parties. Difficult words: Marxist (the social, political, and economic theory of Karl Marx), dispute (a disagreement), ignite (to cause suddenly). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Since 1975, the MPLA party has ruled in Angola when the country became independent from Portugal. Last week, the party won the elections again, but it lost its majority in parliament. Now MPLA must cooperate with the opposition , which never happened before. Experts worry that the situation will upset poor young people who don’t support MPLA. Officials announced the result only one day after the election, which was very unusual. In 2017, people took two weeks to know the results of the vote. Difficult words: elections (the time to vote a person or people for a job in politics), majority (the larger part of something), opposition (a party or parties in a government who speak or fight against the party that is leading). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last week, national elections happen in Angola. The MPLA party wins again. Since 1975, MPLA is the strongest party in the government. That same year, Angola doesn’t belong to Portugal. MPLA rules for nearly 50 years without a break. Something is different now. MPLA doesn’t have a majority in parliament. A majority is when few parties are there. MPLA must rule with them. It will not be an easy situation. Experts think that problems can start. Young people are not happy that MPLA wins. They vote for other parties. Experts say that young people can start protests. Difficult words: elections (the time to choose a person on people for a job in politics), party (a group of people in politics, who work together, and they have the same ideas), rule (to have power over a country and people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

While sailing from Gallipoli to Milazzo in Sicily, a 40-meter super yacht named ‘Saga’ got into trouble. On Saturday night, the captain sent a distress call because the vessel began taking on water at the stern . The Italian coast guard tried to tow the ship back to port; however, the stern completely sank on Sunday morning. Coast guard took all four passengers and five crew members to safety, and their investigation began on why the yacht. Several media said the vessel was linked to Russian oligarch Gennady Ayvazyan; he is the 54-year-old co-owner of Russia’s second largest coal exporter. Italian media believe that the ship was worth at least 50 million dollars, and it was one of the largest yachts built by a Monaco yachting company. Difficult words: distress call (a signal that a ship or plane sends when it needs help), stern (the rear part of a ship), oligarch (a very rich person with political influence, especially in Russia). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A big yacht sank near Italy last weekend. The yacht was on its way to Sicily, and when it was crossing the water, it got into trouble. Water came into the back of the yacht, and the captain called for help. The Italian coast guard arrived to save the yacht, but it sank. The coast guard saved the four passengers and five members of the crew, and they took them to port. Authorities started to investigate why the yacht sank. Some media said that the yacht cost around 50 million dollars, and it belonged to a Russian oligarch . This man is one of the owners of a large coal company in Russia. Difficult words: yacht (a large expensive boat which people use for trips or holidays), oligarch (a very rich person, especially in Russia), coal (a black or brown rock which burns easily). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A big yacht sails in the Mediterranean sea last week. It sails to the Italian island of Sicily. Suddenly, the yacht has problems. Water gets into the back part of the boat. The captain calls for help. The coast guard come. They try to help the boat. They are not successful. Four passengers and five staff are on the boat. They are safe. The boat sinks. Authorities must find out why the boat sinks. Some journalists say that the boat belongs to a rich Russian man. He is 54 years old. He has a coal company in Russia. The yacht costs more than 50 million dollars. Difficult words: yacht (a very big and expensive boat), coast guard (people, who protect the coast, and they help ships which have problems), staff (workers at a specific place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A combat sports centre in Moscow, Russia, invited those feeling vulnerable to learn some new selfie stick defence techniques. As the trainer pointed out, you do not always have a tool at hand, and not everyone can use force in martial arts. Moreover, he thinks that the tool people normally use for taking pictures is very effective. One customer said that she decided to come to the combat class because it was very exciting and because she thinks that it is necessary to know how to protect yourself in a difficult situation. Difficult words: combat (related to fighting), vulnerable (in danger).

The selfie stick is a popular tool for taking pictures, but people can also use it as a method of self-defence. A combat sports centre in Moscow teaches people how to protect themselves with a selfie stick. Not everybody is strong enough to fight, and there isn’t always another tool to use besides a selfie stick. The organisers say that the method can be handy for Russian tourists who are travelling abroad. Difficult words: tool (a thing which is used for doing something), combat (related to fighting), handy (useful). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The selfie stick is popular. You can take pictures with it. You can also protect yourself with it. A combat sports centre in Moscow can teach you! Sometimes, there is nothing better than your selfie stick. It can serve you well in a difficult situation. Difficult words: combat (for fighting), serve well (to be useful – good). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In India’s eastern Siliguri city, unpredictable weather conditions affected tea production. In June, the region faced heavy rains; however, dry weather followed in July, which damaged plants and made hard conditions for workers. They couldn’t pluck leaves during heavy rains, and when the temperature reached 39 degrees Celsius, they still couldn’t work. In addition, insects infected the plantations . Tea plantations in Siliguri always depended on the weather; however, the weather patterns changed and upset the industry’s economics . This year, farmers suffered 25-30% of crop loss. Difficult words: pluck (to remove), plantation (a large farm to grow crops for coffee, sugar, or tobacco), economics (production, distribution and consumption of goods). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Weather changes caused problems for southern Indian tea farmers. In June, heavy rains fell and damaged the plants; in addition, workers couldn’t pick tea leaves in the rain. In July, very hot weather came, and temperatures reached 39 degrees Celsius. The work in tea plantations was too difficult, and farmers also had too many insects in their plants. In India, tea plants depend on the weather. This year’s weather was so unusual and extreme that farmers lost about 25-30% of their crops. Difficult words: plantation (a large farm where farmers grow plants for coffee, sugar, or tobacco), insect (a very small animal with wings and six legs), extreme (very unusual and great). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Weather is more extreme in many parts of the world. Farmers have many problems. Tea farmers in India worry. It rains too much in June. The rain damages plants. Workers can’t pick tea leaves in the rain. More problems come in July. The weather is too hot. Temperatures reach 39 degrees Celsius. Insects live well in the rain and the heat. They damage some plants. The work to grow tea is very difficult. Good weather is important. This year’s weather is very bad for tea plants. Farmers lose many crops . Difficult words: extreme (very unusual), damage (harm), crops (plants which farmers grow). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Epecuen, which is 549 kilometres southwest of Buenos Aires, Argentina, once was a busy lakeside village renowned for its saltwater baths. This came to a sudden end in November 1985, though, when the town’s lake overflowed and water surged into the town. Locals and tourists were forced to evacuate and just days later, their homes and buildings were covered by almost 10 metres of salt water. Now, 30 years on, the village is one of Argentina’s tourist attractions once more; the water has evaporated and former residents can walk through the ruins of what was once their town. It looks like a setting from a zombie apocalypse film. Difficult words: renowned (known by many people), surge (move suddenly and powerfully), evaporate (turn from liquid into vapour/gas), former (-ex). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Epecuen in Argentina was a lakeside village. People knew it for its saltwater baths. In November 1985, however, Epecuen came to a sudden end. The town’s lake overflowed and water surged into the town. People had to leave and saltwater covered the buildings by almost 10 metres. Now, 30 years on, the water evaporated and people can walk through the ruins. The town looks like something from a zombie apocalypse film! Difficult words: surge (to move suddenly and powerfully), evaporate (to turn from liquid into vapour/gas), apocalypse (the complete destruction of the world). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about a village. This village is in Argentina. It is by a saltwater lake. One day, something bad happens. The water rises . People must leave the village. The water covers the village. It is under water for 30 years. Now, the water evaporates . You can visit the village again. It looks very strange . Difficult words: rise (to go up), evaporate (to go away; to change to vapour – gas), strange (not normal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

South Koreans traditionally eat most meals with a generous dollop of the fiery local side dish kimchi , but they are also growing taste for another fermented food – cheese. While Japan is by far the biggest consumer of cheese in Asia, South Korea is one of the fastest growing markets. The USA exported fifty-three per cent of cheese to South Korea in 2015’s first nine months. New Zealand exported 13%, and the rest came from Germany, France and others. Cheese demand has been increased, thanks to exposure to Western dishes such as pizza, but South Koreans also incorporate cheese into local dishes like noodle soup and kimchi stir-fried rice. A possible explanation is that cheese helps to take away the heat from spicy dishes. Cheese consumption is on the rise in the Asian country, but 2.4 kilograms per person per year is still nothing compared to France where people consume ten more times the cheese. Difficult words: dollop (a large amount), fiery (spicy), kimchi (cabbage that has been stored with vinegar), fermented (to last longer after it is changed by bacteria, yeast, or other microorganisms), exposure to (experience with). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Japan is the biggest consumer of cheese in Asia, but South Korea is one of the fastest growing markets . This is because South Koreans are starting to like Western dishes like pizza, but they also like to incorporate cheese into their traditional dishes. They say that cheese takes away the heat from spicy dishes. Per person, South Koreans eat 2.4 kilograms of cheese. It may seem like a lot, but it is only a tenth of the cheese that people eat in France. Difficult words: market (a national or international selling and buying of things), dish (food prepared in a specific way as a meal), incorporate (to include). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about cheese. In Asia, Japan is the biggest consumer of cheese. South Koreans are starting to like cheese, too. They buy more and more of it. They are starting to like Western dishes . They like pizza, for example. They also put cheese into traditional Korean dishes. Every South Korean eats around 2.4 kilograms of cheese. A Frenchman eats 10 times more. Difficult words: consumer (somebody who consumes – eats), dish (food cooked in a specific way), traditional (typical of a country/area). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Near the Israeli city of Tel Aviv, footage showed a bull with a rope hanging from its neck as it ran through a bank’s corridors. On Monday, the incident started in a car park outside the bank, when the huge animal found its way inside the building. The animal slammed into walls as it skidded around corners and workers fled. People attempted to control the bull and to get its attention to get it out of the building. Officials found the bull’s owner and called him to the scene. They also called a vet if needed to tranquilize the animal. The recapture took more than half an hour, and officials said they would investigate where it came from and how it escaped. Difficult words: skid (to slide on the ground after you run or walk too quickly), tranquilize (to drug an animal to calm it or make it unconscious), recapture (the repeated capture of an escaped person or animal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Monday, people saw a big bull running through a car park near Tel Aviv, Israel. He had a rope around his neck, so they knew that the animal ran away from somewhere. The bull managed to get inside a bank. CCTV cameras caught the bull as it ran in the hall, when suddenly, it hit a wall. The animal was confused and kept running. Some people tried to stop the bull, and one man even shouted at the animal to catch its attention . Officials found the owner, and he and a vet came to be ready to tranquilize the bull. No one knew how the bull escaped and from where. People took more than 30 minutes to catch the animal. Difficult words: CCTV (a system of screens and cameras inside a building or in a public place), attention (a time to watch, listen, or think about something), tranquilize (to give a person or animal a drug to calm him or makes him fall asleep). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Something unusual happens near Tel Aviv, Israel. People see a bull in a car park. The bull runs among the cars. It is very fast and angry. Then, the animal runs into a bank. People in the bank are scared. They run away. The bull slides on the floor. It hits a wall. Some people try to stop the animal. Officials find the owner of the animal. The owner comes to the place. Officials call a vet , too. People catch the bull. It is not easy. They take more than 30 minutes. No one knows how the bull escapes and from where. Difficult words: slide (to move on the ground without control because of water or ice), owner (a person who has something), vet (an animal doctor). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Andrew Tate appeared on the 2016 season of UK Big Brother; recently, the show’s managers evicted him after a social media video appeared of him beating a woman outside the show. Since then, Tate claimed the video was a joke, but Instagram and Facebook recently banned him. Facebook said he could radicalize men and boys to harm women. Twitter banned him because he said women should bear responsibility for sexual assault. Before Instagram removed his account, Tate had 4.7 million followers on the platform. He offered his mostly male fans tips to make money and attract women. In an interview with a YouTuber, Tate described himself as a misogynist . However, he said he only played a character in his videos, and he was innocent. He is still on YouTube with over 750,000 subscribers. Difficult words: evict (to force someone to leave a place), radicalize (to make someone be extreme in his political or religious beliefs), misogynist (a person who hates women and thinks men are much better than them). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Andrew Tate is an American-British internet personality and a former professional kickboxer. In 2016, Tate appeared in the UK Big Brother show, but he had to leave because someone posted a video of him which showed him beating a woman. He said that the video was only a joke and that he did nothing wrong. Tate had 4.7 million followers on Instagram. This summer, Instagram canceled his account this summer, while Facebook and Twitter also banned him. In his videos, he gave men tips on how to make money and how to be with a woman who they liked. He called himself a misogynist and said that it was women’s faults if they got sexually attacked. Although some social media said that Tate was dangerous because he could change men’s opinions on women, he was still active on YouTube with over 750,000 subscribers . Difficult words: personality (a character), misogynist (a person who hates women), subscriber (a person who pays to get a product or service). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Andrew Tate is an American-British influencer . He is a kickboxer in the past, too. In 2016, Tate is in the UK Big Brother show. Someone shows a video of him. The video shows him when is beating a woman. Tate must leave the show. He says that the video is only a joke. He says that he does nothing wrong. Surprisingly, Tate says that he hates women. He says a woman does something wrong if a person attacks her. Hundreds of thousands of men watch his videos on social media. Facebook says that Tate is dangerous. Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter ban him. He still has over 750,000 subscribers on YouTube. Difficult words: influencer (a person who can change the thoughts and ideas of other people, usually on social media), ban (to stop something officially), subscriber (a person who pays to get a product or service). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Israeli archaeologists unearthed what they think is an ancient Greek fortress in Jerusalem, which archaeologists have been looking for for more than two centuries. Historians say that the 250-metre-long and 60-metre-wide fortress is where rebels took back Jerusalem from the Greeks, a victory marked in the Jewish holiday of Hanukkah. The debate over the location of the 2,000-year-old acra has seen many claims that it stood in Jerusalem’s Old City at spots like the Christian Church of the Holy Sepulchre near where Jewish temples also lay, but the most recently unearthed remains are outside the walls overlooking an area known as the City of David. Difficult words: unearth (dig out of the ground), acra (a Greek fortress from a long time ago), claims (what people say and may be true) You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People found a 2,000-year-old fortress in Jerusalem. It is around 250 metres long and 60 metres wide. People were looking for this fortress for more than two centuries. Two thousand years ago, there were Greeks in the region. Historians say that the fortress is where Jewish rebels took Jerusalem back from the Greeks. The holiday of Hanukkah marks this victory . Difficult words: fortress (a large, strong building for protection), mark (to show something is special), victory (when you win). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Around 2,000 years ago, there were Greeks in Jerusalem. The Jews fought the Greeks. The Jews won. They took a fortress from the Greeks. People try to find this fortress. They try for 2,000 years. Now, they finally find it. It is 250 metres long and 60 metres wide. Difficult words: were (past of “are”), fought (past of “fight”), fortress (a strong building for protection). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Footage was captured of a great white shark jumping out of the water to grab a seal off the coast of Massachusetts. The seal managed to get away, but there were many sightings of the big predator that summer, so it might have eventually been prey. Great white sharks grow up to 6 metres in length and can weigh more than 2 tonnes. The man who captured the video was working with the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy in Cape Cod when he recorded the footage, and he said that people had tagged two more great whites in that area. Both were about 3.7 metres long. Difficult words: grab (to catch), sighting (an instance of seeing something special), tag (to put a tag on something – to identify it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Great white sharks grow up to 6 metres in length and weigh more than 2 tonnes. This summer, there were many sightings of them off the Massachusetts coast in the USA. One video shows how a shark eyed its prey and jumped out of the water to catch a seal. It looked, however, that the seal was lucky and escaped. Difficult words: sighting (an instance of seeing something special), eye (to watch), prey (an animal which is hunted and killed for food). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Great white sharks can be 6 metres long. They can be 2 tonnes heavy. Many people see great white sharks in Massachusetts. Massachusetts is on the east coast of the USA. One video is really cool. It shows a great white shark. The shark hunts a seal . The seal jumps out of the water. The shark jumps out, too. It tries to catch the seal. The seal is lucky. The shark does not catch it. Difficult words: coast (the part of the land near the sea), hunt (to try to catch, kill and eat), seal (an animal which feeds its babies with milk, rests on land and catches fish in the water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An alleged car thief in Australia chose an unusual way to attempt to avoid the law. Following a two-hour car chase in Perth, the man stopped the vehicle to deflate the tyre pressure before driving towards the beach. He then drove into the ocean. As the vehicle began to sink, the man climbed out of a window and attempted to swim off. Officers were forced to wade into the waves in order to catch their suspect whose out-of-the-box escape tactic ultimately failed. Difficult words: alleged (so-called by some people), attempt (to try), deflate (to let out some gas), tyre (a thick rubber ring that fits around the wheel of a car), wade (to walk through water that is not deep), out-of-the-box (unusual and creative). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Police in Perth, Australia were chasing a man. After two hours, the man drove towards the beach. He stopped at the beach for a moment. When the police car arrived, he drove into the ocean. The unusual tactic, however, did not work. His car began to sink, so he climbed out of a window and tried to swim away. Police officers waded into the water and caught him. Difficult words: chase (to follow and to try to catch), arrive (to come), wade (to walk in water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Perth. Perth is in Australia. Police chase a man. The man drives towards the beach. He stops at the beach. The police car arrives . The man drives into the ocean. His car begins to sink . He gets out of the car. He tries to swim away, but the police catch him. Difficult words: chase (to follow and to try to catch), arrive (to come), sink (to go down in water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At least 12 people, mostly civilians, died in a hotel siege in the Somali capital of Mogadishu. On Friday evening Al-Qaeda affiliate Al-Shabab detonated at least two bombs outside the hotel before they entered. Rescuers saved some guests and staff members; however, an unknown number of gunmen seized hostages , and they held them inside the hotel. Al-Shabab has a long-running conflict with the Somali government; the hotel was a popular location for government employees to meet. The group controls much of southern and central Somalia, and it’s extending its influence into government areas. In recent weeks, Al-Shabab attacked targets along the Somalia-Ethiopia border, which raised concerns about its new activity. The attack was the group’s first in the capital since May and the election of Somalia’s new president Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. Difficult words: siege (a situation when an armed force surrounds a place), affiliate (a group or organization connected or controlled by a larger one), hostage (a person who an enemy holds so that he can get something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Friday, Al-Shabab militants attacked a hotel in Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia. Al-Shabab is part of Al-Qaeda, and Al-Shabab controls a large part of southern and central Somalia. The government controls the other parts, but some people worry that Al-Shabab also wants these parts. The attackers exploded two bombs outside the hotel, and then they ran inside. Many people escaped, but the militants took some hostages , and they killed at least 12 people. 24 hours later, officials were still working on the situation, and the attackers were still inside the hotel. Last week’s attack was the first since May when people elected the new president. Difficult words: militant (a person who works as an unofficial soldier), hostage (a person who another person holds to get something), elect (to choose someone for a job in politics). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A group of men attack a hotel in Mogadishu. The city is the capital of Somalia. Politicians often meet in this hotel. The attack happens last Friday. Two bombs explode outside the hotel. The attackers run inside. They kill 12 people. They hold some people hostage . Some people run away. Nobody really knows how many attackers are in the hotel. They belong to Al-Shabab. Al-Shabab is a militant group . It is a part of Al-Qaeda. Al-Shabab controls southern and central Somalia. It fights against the government . Al-Shabab may want to control other parts of the country. Difficult words: hostage (a person who somebody traps to get something), militant group (a group of people believe something so strongly that they fight for it), government (the people who lead a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lexus created the world’s first drivable cardboard car. The unique model is an exact replica of Toyota’s IS Saloon, and people pieced it together from precisely -cut pieces of cardboard. The car comes with a fully- fitted interior, functioning doors, headlights and rolling wheels. Difficult words: precisely (done in a very exact, careful way), fitted (equipped). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Lexus created the first drivable cardboard car in the world. It is a life-size replica of Toyota’s new IS Saloon. You can enter the car and move it backwards and forwards. It is something quite special. Difficult words: cardboard (thick brown paper; the material in the picture), replica (an exact copy of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lexus creates a special car. It is made from cardboard . The car is a replica of a Toyota. The replica is as big as the original. The car works. You can enter it and move it. Difficult words: create (to make), cardboard (thick brown paper; the material in the picture), replica (a copy of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scotland is the first country in the world to legislate free period products for women and girls in need. In the current cost of the living crisis, this law makes a huge difference, as women will get free period products in schools, colleges, and many other venues . So far, women and girls accessed free products through food banks if they couldn’t afford to buy them. Some women and girls said they used period products for longer than is safe or hygienic, which caused a lot of exclusion . Difficult words: venue (a place for a service or event), food bank (a place with food for poor people), exclusion (a situation when a person cannot go to a place or do an activity). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Right now, many products are more expensive, and for some women, they cannot buy period products. Scotland became the first country to make a law for free period products for women and girls. They can get period products at schools, shopping centers, or other places. Before the new law, poor women could ask food banks for help. Some women have so little money that they can’t buy these products every month. Sometimes, they use the products longer than is safe or hygienic . For this reason, they can’t do all activities or go to all places. Difficult words: period (once a month, blood comes from a woman’s body), food bank (a place with food for poor people), hygienic (clean). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Women and girls have a period every month. The period is when blood comes out of their body. Women who are not pregnant have a period. Some women and girls don’t have enough money to buy period products. They get help from food banks . Sometimes they cannot get help. Some women use period products longer than is safe or clean. These women cannot do some activities or go to some places. They stay at home. Scotland makes a new law. All women can get free period products. These products will be in schools, shopping centers, and other places. Scotland is the first country in the world with this law. Difficult words: pregnant (a baby inside a woman’s body), food bank (a place with food for poor people), free (costs no money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NASA launched a new website featuring images of the full, sunlit side of the earth taken by a camera located one million miles away. The Earth Polychromatic Imaging Camera captures the earth as it orbits for a new project between NASA and other American agencies. The project’s objective is to maintain real-time solar wind monitoring, which is crucial for weather alerts and forecasts. Each day, NASA will post images showing the Earth as it rotates. Difficult words: launch (to start something), feature (to have something), polychromatic (colourful), objective (something which you want to achieve), solar wind (a flow of charged particles from the sun), crucial (very important). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

NASA launched a new website. It features colour images of the full, sunlit side of the Earth. A NASA camera takes the images and it is 1.6 million kilometres away. Each day, NASA will post images from 12 to 36 hours earlier. You can see how the Earth rotates. Difficult words: launch (to start), feature (to have), post (to upload, to put on a website). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NASA launches a new website. There are colour images of the Earth on the website. A NASA camera takes the images. The camera is 1.6 million kilometres from the Earth. In the images, you can see how the Earth rotates . Difficult words: launch (to start), Earth (the planet where we live), rotate (to move in a circle). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The cost of the living crisis is worsening, leading some UK pet owners to give up their animals to save money. UK’s famous Battersea charity is currently caring for hundreds of dogs and cats, and similar centers around the country say they’re receiving record inquiries for dog and cat returns. Many owners say the additional cost of food and veterinary care isn’t manageable. One owner came to the charity to return a pregnant cat because he was no longer able to afford to care for the cat and her unborn kittens. The trend follows a surge in demand for pets during the COVID-19 pandemic. UK households are dealing with a huge crisis in their energy bills, and experts warn a recession is going to come. Some charities warn it can put millions of people into poverty , and they hope that someone will be able to give the animals permanent homes. Difficult words: inquiry (an informational question), recession (low economic activity), poverty (very poor). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, people spent more time at home, and many of them got a dog or cat. Now, people in the UK have problems because the pet care is too expensive. Food and vet bills cost more. Many pet owners are giving up the animals, and animal rescue centers are getting full. Experts warn that a crisis will come. Millions of people may not have enough money for living. Charities hope someone will look after their animals. Difficult words: vet (an animal doctor), animal rescue center (a place for animals which are ill or which someone can’t look after), crisis (a difficult or dangerous time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People spend more time at home during the coronavirus. They don’t want to be alone. They get a dog or cat. Now, prices are getting higher. Care for pets is more expensive. In the UK, many people don’t want their pet anymore. They don’t have money for food for their pets. Also, animal doctors are expensive. Animal rescue centers are full of dogs and cats. People bring animals to them every day. Experts say that a more difficult time will come. Many people will be poor . They hope that someone will care for the dogs and cats. Difficult words: pet (an animal which lives with people), animal rescue center (a place for ill animals or animals, which need a home), poor (very little money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Tour operators are creating chaos as they overcrowd and overbook in Machu Picchu, Peru’s most popular tourist destination. Machu Picchu’s long lines and crowds forced authorities to halt ticket sales until the end of the week. The measure stranded foreign and local tourists. Unable to reach the site, hundreds of them blocked nearby rail tracks to protest. Machu Picchu has a maximum capacity of 4,044 people per day; however, Peru’s culture minister warned of local tour operators who sell counterfeit tickets. Some tour operators ask passengers to take the train and buy tickets on arrival at the site; however, no one will be there for them. The country’s tourism minister said that the number of visitors would increase to 5,044 per day, which frustrated local people. In the 15th century, the Incan people built the citadel , and in 2018, it attracted 1.5 million visitors. Difficult words: measure (an action to end something), counterfeit (fake), citadel (a castle or fortress to protect people). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Machu Picchu is an ancient Incan city in Peru, and it is the country’s most popular destination. In 2018, 1.5 million tourists visited the site, and when the pandemic ended, even more people were keen to visit. The place became too crowded, and tourists waited in long lines. Last week, local authorities stopped the sale of tickets for over one week. Some tourists became very angry. Tour operators asked visitors to come by bus or train to Machu Picchu and then buy tickets. Some of them protested against that they couldn’t come. Officials warned tourists against operators who sold fake or too many tickets. Machu Picchu had a rule for 4,044 people to visit in one day. Officials plan to increase the number to 5,044 people, but local people don’t agree. Difficult words: tour operator (a company which sells tours and holidays), fake (not real), increase (to make something bigger or greater). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A lady on holiday in the Bahamas never expected to see her phone again when she dropped it into the ocean. However, as she was at a dolphin encounter, a dolphin named Cacique retrieved the phone from the seabed in moments. Unfortunately, the tourist’s iPhone was not waterproof and the brisk rescue mission was in vain . Difficult words: retrieve (to find something and bring it back), brisk (quick), in vain (without success). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Unfortunately, the phone was already dead. Difficult words: encounter (meeting), retrieve (to find something and bring it back), seabed (the ocean floor). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Results of a study released in 2015 shows a 49% decline in the number of marine species around the world between 1970 and 2012. The study of marine mammals, ranging from birds to reptiles to fish, highlighted that marine life is disappearing faster than conservationists had feared. The figure is actually 10% higher than previous estimates. The decline is not only bad news for ecosystems but to humans as well, especially to people in the developing world who depend on the ocean’s resources. As stated in the report, the blame for halving global fish stocks falls heavily on over-fishing and climate change, with the deep-sea fish population down 72%. Rising water temperatures and increasing acidity have left 3/4 of coral reefs under threat, and it is possible that most coral reefs could die out by 2050. People also fear that a quarter of the world’s sharks, rays and skates could eventually become extinct. Difficult words: marine (relating to the sea), species (a type of animal), figure (a number), spell (mean), stock (investment), ray (a big fish that moves in the water like a bird), skate (a type of a ray). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

This is bad news for the animals, as well as people. Many people need the ocean to make a living. The reason for this is rising water temperatures, over-fishing and climate change. Experts say that we could lose the coral reefs from most areas by 2050. Difficult words: marine (relating to the sea), species (a type of animal), decline (to become less). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The water is getting warmer. The climate is changing. Also, people fish too much. Difficult words: study (a text written by scientists about something), marine (the sea), climate (the typical weather of an area). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Johnson&Johnson is the world’s largest healthcare company; in 2023, it will stop its global sale of its controversial talc baby powder. The change is happening more than two years after the company ended sales of the product in the US and Canada. The baby powder drew about 38,000 consumer lawsuits over alleged materials that cause cancer, and the product’s demand felt. Johnson&Johnson denied all allegations and called them misinformation; however, last week, it announced that it would shift to a cornstarch baby powder. They already sell it in several countries around the world. Johnson&Johnson repeatedly said that its talc products were safe, and they didn’t cause cancer; however, people found evidence the company knew asbestos was present in its products for decades. Difficult words: talc (a soft, grey mineral with a soapy feel), cornstarch (a flour made from corn or maize that people usually use as a thickener in cooking), asbestos (a heat resistant mineral with long and thin fibers). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Two years ago, the company Johnson&Johnson stopped the sale of its baby powder in the US and Canada. In 2023, the company will stop the sale of it in all the world. Customers sent more than 38,000 lawsuits to Johnson&Johnson; they said that the baby powder was dangerous because it contained asbestos , and it could cause cancer. Many people did not buy it because they were scared to use it. Johnson&Johnson repeatedly said that the product was safe for children. Then, journalists found that the company knew for many years that the powder was dangerous. Last week, Johnson&Johnson said that it will make a new baby powder with safe ingredients . Difficult words: lawsuit (a legal action or complaint), asbestos (a thing with long thin fibers which can cause cancer), ingredient (one of the things inside of a product). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
